html:
The Vandal Kingdom was a Germanic kingdom in North Africa, centred on Carthage, from 435 to 534. It is shown here in 500. The Vandals had come a long way: from central Europe, across the Rhine into Gaul in the crossing of 406, through Spain, and over the strait to Africa in 429.

Under King Gaiseric they took Roman Africa, the richest grain land of the Western Empire. Saint Augustine died during their siege of Hippo in 430. They took Carthage in 439, built a fleet, ruled Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica, and in 455 sacked Rome for two weeks.

The Vandals were Arian Christians and often persecuted the Catholic majority. Their kingdom weakened after Gaiseric died in 477, and Berber kingdoms grew in the interior. In 533 the eastern emperor Justinian sent Belisarius, who destroyed the kingdom within months in the Vandalic War.
